segments.t: This tab configures toolbar icon size, window geometry behavior, dashboard state retention, the frame around the terminal of a colored connection, whether terminal tabs take the title the shell sets, the order in which KTPH003KTPH001KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH002KTPH006 switches tabs, and what korTTY does at startup with the windows and tabs that were open before. Open via KTPH007Configuration → Global Settings → WindowKTPH008; stored in KTPH000.
Frame the terminal in its connection's tab color
Frame the split pane the keyboard is in
Name terminal tabs after the title the shell sets
Ctrl+Tab switches tabs in the order they were last used
Offer to restore the previous session / Restore the previous session automatically / Do nothing
Offer to restore the previous session
Also restore the output of each terminal pane (encrypted)

With KTPH000Remember window geometryKTPH001 enabled, KorTTY stores the position and size of every user-resizable application window and named dialog separately. Reopening a window restores the geometry chosen for that window type; if its previous monitor is no longer connected, KorTTY moves it back onto an available screen, and a main window that was maximized opens maximized there. On macOS, a main window's saved bounds are reapplied after its native unified title bar is ready so the system cannot shift the restored position while opening it. A changed UI font scale keeps the remembered position but lets the window calculate a fresh size so translated or enlarged labels still fit. Short-lived confirmations and progress notices keep their content-derived size.

When KTPH000Use fixed window geometryKTPH001 is enabled, it takes precedence over KTPH002Remember window geometryKTPH003 for main terminal windows. Dialogs continue to use their own remembered geometry.
The KTPH000Remember dashboard stateKTPH001 setting preserves whether the dashboard panel was open or closed the last time you closed the application, and restores that state on the next launch.

With KTPH000Open tool windows as tabsKTPH001 enabled, management tools (Snippets, JobScheduler, AI Manager, Saved Chats, Session Journals, Credential/GPG/SSH key management, Video Manager, Teamwork settings, Terminal Effects) open as tabs in the main window instead of separate windows. The tab opens in the window whose menu you used, so with several main windows open each window collects its own tool tabs. Reopening a tool focuses its existing tab. The Snippet Manager is one tab per main window and opens the snippets you edit as tabs inside itself; a snippet editor opened from elsewhere (for example the SFTP Manager, the file browser or the terminal) and the session journal viewer open a new main-window tab each time, but a snippet that is already open in an editor is brought to the front instead of opening twice. The Full code analysis is a side panel inside the snippet editor, not a tab of its own. The setting takes effect the next time a tool is opened.
A tool hosted as a tab has no separate window geometry. Its available size follows the main window and its saved main-window geometry.

KTPH000Toolbar icon size (px)KTPH001 changes the vector icons in the action toolbar, connection toolbar and customization catalog. Move the slider to see the example icon and pixel value update immediately; this preview does not change the saved value. Save to apply it immediately to every open window; it also survives restarts. Existing configurations keep the 24 px default. The toolbar and catalog adapt their button sizes and keep at least two complete catalog rows visible.

KTPH000Frame the terminal in its connection's tab colorKTPH001 draws a 3-pixel frame around the terminal of every tab whose connection has a KTPH002tab colorKTPH003, in addition to the colored dot on the tab, so a production server stands out right where you type. The frame surrounds the whole tab content — all split panes and the status bars below them — and connections without a tab color never get one. A split pane opened to a connection whose tab color differs from the tab's gets a frame of its own color at its edge, which does not resize its terminal (see KTPH004Tab colorKTPH005). Switch the setting off to keep only the dot; it removes the panes' frames as well. The change applies to the open tabs of every window as soon as you save.

The frame takes 3 pixels on each side of the terminal. Turning it on or off therefore resizes the open terminals of every colored connection, and giving a connection a tab color or removing it resizes that connection's terminals: the remote side receives the new size, and full-screen programs such as KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002 redraw.

KTPH000Frame the split pane the keyboard is inKTPH001 shows the KTPH002focus ringKTPH003 in a tab with two or more split panes: a blue ring around the pane you type into and a dimmer one around the pane the menu commands act on while the keyboard is elsewhere. Switch it off to drop both rings; the active pane then shows only by its cursor. The ring never resizes a terminal, and switching it off leaves the frames in a connection's tab color in place. The change applies to the open tabs of every window as soon as you save.

KTPH001Name terminal tabs after the title the shell setsKTPH002 lets a terminal tab show the title that the shell or another program in it sets with the OSC 0 or OSC 2 escape sequence, such as KTPH000, in place of the connection's name; a tab with split panes shows the title of its focused pane. A name you gave a tab with KTPH003Rename TabKTPH004 still comes first. The server decides this title, so it is cleaned of control and bidi characters, capped at 80 characters and never changes the tab color; pointing at such a tab shows the connection it belongs to. Switch it off to keep the connection's names on every tab. The change applies to the open tabs of every window as soon as you save. See KTPH005Title from the shellKTPH006.

KTPH015Ctrl+Tab switches tabs in the order they were last usedKTPH016 changes what KTPH017KTPH000KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH001KTPH020 and KTPH021KTPH002KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH003KTPH024+KTPH025KTPH004KTPH026 do (KTPH027KTPH005KTPH028 on macOS too). Off, they go to the next and the previous tab of the tab bar. On, KTPH029KTPH006KTPH030+KTPH031KTPH007KTPH032 goes back to the tab you used before the current one, so one press switches between your two latest tabs. Keep KTPH033KTPH008KTPH034 held and press KTPH035KTPH009KTPH036 again to go further back through the tabs, from the most to the least recently used, add KTPH037KTPH010KTPH038 to step the other way, and release KTPH039KTPH011KTPH040 at the tab you want; KTPH041KTPH012KTPH042+KTPH043KTPH013KTPH044+KTPH045KTPH014KTPH046 on its own starts at the tab you used longest ago. Only the tab you stop at counts as used, so the tabs you pass on the way keep their places in the order. Pressing any other key, choosing a tab with the mouse or switching to another window also ends the step-through at the tab it reached, and the key you pressed then acts on that tab. The order is the one the KTPH047command paletteKTPH048 lists the tabs in: it lasts as long as the window and is never saved. The change applies to every window as soon as you save; the palette's KTPH049Next TabKTPH050 and KTPH051Previous TabKTPH052 follow it too.
KTPH000At startup:KTPH001 decides what korTTY does with the windows and tabs that were open before this start, which it keeps in the KTPH002session snapshotKTPH003 while it runs:

KTPH000Offer to restore the previous sessionKTPH001 (the default) shows a bar above the status line of the window with KTPH002RestoreKTPH003 and KTPH004DismissKTPH005, for example KTPH006Restore the windows and tabs from before this start? Windows: 2, tabs: 6KTPH007. It never blocks the window, and nothing opens until you choose KTPH008RestoreKTPH009.

KTPH000Restore the previous session automaticallyKTPH001 reopens them by itself as soon as no dialog is open, so the questions their connections may ask never come on top of another dialog; if a dialog stays open for a minute, korTTY offers them in the bar instead.
KTPH000Do nothingKTPH001 shows nothing at startup.

KTPH002File → Restore Previous SessionKTPH003 opens the previous session in every mode. Either way the tabs open without asking anything: a tab that needs a password, a new temporary SSH key or the locked vault waits in the KTPH004restore barKTPH005. If korTTY ends unexpectedly within a minute of a restore, the next start offers the session instead of restoring it automatically, so a session that makes korTTY crash cannot do so at every start. A missing or unknown value in KTPH000 means KTPH006Offer to restore the previous sessionKTPH007, so a damaged file never opens connections by itself. Your organization can set the mode with the KTPH001 key of its KTPH008enterprise policyKTPH009; the dropdown is then locked with the "Managed by your organization" hint. The setting takes effect at the next start. See KTPH010At startupKTPH011.

KTPH001Also restore the output of each terminal pane (encrypted)KTPH002 keeps the newest lines of every terminal pane with the session snapshot, and a restored tab or pane shows them again, dimmed and above its new session; they are only shown on your computer, never sent to the server or typed into the shell. It is off by default, because terminal output can hold secrets: korTTY writes it only encrypted with the key of your master password, readable only by you and never into backups or project files. Without a master password, or while the vault is locked, nothing is saved or restored, and the status bar says so when a restore finds saved output it cannot read. KTPH003Lines of output per paneKTPH004 sets how many of the newest lines are kept, from 100 to 5000. Turning the option off deletes the saved output at once, and so do a change of the master password and restoring a backup. Your organization can set the option with the KTPH000 key of its KTPH005enterprise policyKTPH006; the switch and the lines are then locked with the "Managed by your organization" hint. See KTPH007Restoring the outputKTPH008.
